pages.title: Introducing Mistral Large 4
pages.what_its_about: Mistral AI has announced the public preview of 'Mistral Large 4', a next-generation open-weight multimodal model featuring 1 trillion parameters and 52 billion active parameters.
key_points: Mistral Large 4 (ML4) is a native multimodal model that delivers state-of-the-art open model performance across enterprise environments, including coding, agent workflows, cybersecurity, and finance.
Trained from scratch using 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in its proprietary European data centers, it incorporates training data spanning over 160 languages.
Currently available as a preview API via Mistral Studio, the model weights are scheduled for public release at the end of this month following red-teaming and related testing.
notable_data_or_quotes: 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal model with 52 billion active parameters
3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs
Weights drop end of this month
spanning more than 160 languages
pages.intended_audience: AI developers, cybersecurity professionals, enterprise infrastructure and LLM adoption leads

pages.title: Introducing Timestral
pages.what_its_about: Mistral has unveiled 'Timestral', a family of time-series foundation models offering outstanding efficiency and zero-shot performance.
key_points: With a maximum size of 209M parameters, it achieved first place on three major benchmarks—GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench—using only two-thirds of the parameters of previous top-performing models.
Available in four sizes (5M, 28M, 123M, and 209M), it runs efficiently even on CPUs and delivers an optimal balance between accuracy and computational cost.
Combining synthetic data pretraining, covariate-aware attention, and long-context training, it supports multivariate probabilistic forecasting with both past and future covariates.
notable_data_or_quotes: 5M to 209M parameters
GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench
outperforming the previous state of the art with only two-thirds of the model parameters
pages.intended_audience: Enterprise data scientists, industrial engineers, and financial analysts requiring time-series forecasting and analysis

pages.title: Hallo, Deutschland!
pages.what_its_about: French AI company Mistral establishes a new hub in Munich, Germany—Europe's largest industrial economy—and officially expands into Physics AI and industrial AI sectors.
key_points: Mistral opened its Munich hub to bolster competitiveness by combining its capabilities with Germany's manufacturing and industrial expertise across automotive, energy, and aerospace sectors.

Building on physics and engineering AI specialists who joined following the acquisition of Emmi AI in May 2026, Mistral is co-developing crash simulations with BMW and industrial AI applications with Siemens Energy.

To secure European AI sovereignty, Mistral aims to build 1 gigawatt (GW) of European computing infrastructure by 2030 and provide open-weight proprietary model environments running on customer infrastructure.
notable_data_or_quotes: To secure Europe’s AI sovereignty, Mistral will build one gigawatt of European compute capacity by 2030.
Following our acquisition of Emmi AI in May 2026, more than 30 physicists, researchers, and engineers with unique expertise in Physics and Engineering AI joined Mistral.

pages.title: Nobody is safe from celebrity AI deepfakes
pages.what_its_about: AI deepfake images and videos misappropriating celebrity likenesses are spreading on a massive scale by exploiting loopholes in social media verification badge systems, causing severe harm.
key_points: Shortly after actress Mia Goth's divorce, a fan account bearing a paid Instagram blue verification checkmark posted fabricated AI images that garnered hundreds of thousands of 'likes' and spread across the entertainment industry and search engines.
As Meta operates a paid verification badge system, non-public figures' accounts have been mistaken for official accounts, leading to manipulated AI content gaining credibility and circulating widely.
As seen in cases involving Scarlett Johansson, Drake, and others, pushback and legal action from celebrities against impersonation and digital replication using generative AI continue to mount.
notable_data_or_quotes: The @miagoth_ account had over 1 million followers, and the AI post in question recorded approximately 500,000 'likes'.
Christine Tripicchio: "The fact that this fan account qualifies for Instagram's 'blue check' at a foundational level is deeply baffling."

Christine Tripicchio: "Beyond that, it is baffling that Instagram appears to blatantly prioritize the dissemination of fabricated and manipulated images over protecting the publicity rights and integrity of public figures."
pages.intended_audience: Social media users, the general public, and industry professionals interested in AI ethics, publicity rights, and deepfake regulation

pages.title: Artificiality's First Exam: An LLM-Referenced C-test for Supraintelligence
pages.what_its_about: This study proposes a new C-test benchmark combining Large Language Models (LLMs) and Levin's Kt complexity to evaluate supraintelligence that surpasses the capabilities of humans and existing AI.
key_points: Existing benchmarks have limitations in that their difficulty levels are calibrated against humans or current AI, leading to rapid saturation or circular referencing issues.

By combining Levin's Kt—a computable variant of Kolmogorov complexity—with LLMs as representation machines, the authors established a pipeline to generate and verify high-difficulty evaluation questions measured on a ratio scale in bits.

Evaluating certified questions across 12 LLMs confirmed performance degradation curves as difficulty increased, demonstrating the feasibility of evaluating questions in the supraintelligence domain beyond current frontier intelligence.
notable_data_or_quotes: Tested on 12 LLMs
pages.intended_audience: Researchers in AI benchmarking and model evaluation, as well as theoretical researchers in AGI/supraintelligence

pages.title: The Silent Failures in Agentic Data Science
pages.what_its_about: This study points out and systematically analyzes methodological flaws, such as data leakage and validation errors, hidden beneath the surface of simple predictive accuracy evaluations in existing data science agents.
key_points: Conventional evaluations of downstream predictive performance and code correctness alone fail to detect methodological failures such as data leakage and improper validation.

An analysis of 220 data science tasks revealed that regardless of the complexity of the agent framework or model performance, at least one failure mode was found across the vast majority of agent solutions.
A positive correlation was observed between the occurrence of data leakage flaws and predictive performance, proving that a principled analysis of defects beyond mere accuracy is essential.
Compared to expert solutions, such as those from Kaggle competition winners, data science agents were found to generally lack problem-solving creativity and domain expertise.
notable_data_or_quotes: 220 data science tasks
six specific failures
pages.intended_audience: Data science researchers, LLM-based agent system developers, and machine learning engineers

pages.title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop
pages.what_its_about: This study proposes ClawLoop, a harness-native self-improving agent framework that generates tasks, trains, diagnoses, and enhances its performance autonomously without external teacher models or human intervention.
key_points: Introduces a self-feedback iterative structure to overcome the external teacher dependency and one-shot limitations of existing harness-based agent training.
ClawLoop operates through a 3-stage continuous loop: Task Synthesis, Model Training (SFT/RL), and Diagnosis and Feedback.
Tasks refined through the loop model transferred effectively to smaller models, proving the versatility and high quality of the synthesized data.
notable_data_or_quotes: Achieved consistent performance gains across SkillsBench, Claw-Eval-Live, and ClawGym-Bench using Qwen3.6-27B as the loop model
Confirmed benchmark-wide performance improvements in transfer experiments to smaller models, Qwen3.5-4B and 9B
pages.intended_audience: Developers of LLM-based autonomous agents and researchers in AI self-improvement reinforcement learning

pages.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
pages.what_its_about: This study proposes Correction Training, a framework for diffusion models that bridges the exposure bias gap between training and inference to improve generation quality and prevent error accumulation.
key_points: Introduces a corrector step to refine intermediate predictions, mitigating exposure bias and error accumulation during the iterative sampling process of diffusion models.

Significantly improves FID scores for unconditional and unguided generation across DiT, SiT, and JiT architectures, while alleviating oversaturation and enhancing diversity when combined with classifier-free guidance (CFG).
Demonstrates that distilling the refined predictions back into the base diffusion model maintains the improved quality without incurring additional inference-time overhead.
notable_data_or_quotes: DiT, SiT, JiT
pages.intended_audience: Generative AI researchers and deep learning engineers interested in improving diffusion model generation quality and addressing exposure bias issues

pages.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0: Automating Diverse Task Construction and Measuring Sustained Agent Progress
pages.what_its_about: LHTB 2.0, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' ability to sustain continuous task execution in long-horizon terminal environments, has been released.
key_points: LHTB 2.0 was constructed by expanding the existing 46 tasks with 31 new tasks, resulting in a total of 77 tasks across 13 domains and 8 task types.
The evaluation duration was extended from 90 minutes to 3 hours, recording verification checkpoints every 30 minutes to measure intermediate progress via dense progress ladders.

Evaluating 15 frontier models showed that GPT-6-astra scored the highest, demonstrating that outcome-only evaluations substantially overlook intermediate progress compared to fine-grained evaluation scores (0.653 vs. a simple binary evaluation of 0.221).
notable_data_or_quotes: 77 tasks across 13 domains and eight task types
Evaluation time: expanded from 90 minutes to 3 hours, checkpoints recorded every 30 minutes
1,145 scored model-task runs across 15 frontier models
GPT-6-astra: dense mean reward 0.69, 37 tasks with R >= 0.95
GPT-5.6-sol: dense mean reward 0.67, 32 tasks with R >= 0.95
30 reconstructed tasks: binary verifier scores average 0.221 vs dense ladder scores average 0.653
pages.intended_audience: AI agent researchers, LLM evaluation framework developers, and long-running agent system engineers

pages.title: Lotus: Learning to Understand Time-series by Learning to Forecast
pages.what_its_about: Proposes the principle of 'forecast grounding', which pre-trains time-series language models to maintain future-forecasting capabilities, alongside the LOTUS model that implements it.
key_points: To overcome the limitation of existing time-series language models failing to preserve the evolutionary dynamics of time-series signals, introduced the forecast grounding principle that maintains future predictability prior to downstream task adaptation.

LOTUS partitions time-series channels into patches, maps them into the LLM embedding space, predicts the next patch, and employs a time-spectral patch representation method that simultaneously captures temporal dynamics and periodic patterns.
Achieved the highest average performance across 3 language model backbones and 6 benchmark datasets with minimal trainable parameters, outperforming models 25 to 50 times larger on TSRBench.
notable_data_or_quotes: 59.91% accuracy
Outperformed the strongest matching baseline by 3.36%
Outperformed models 25-50x larger on TSRBench
pages.intended_audience: AI researchers and machine learning engineers studying time-series data analysis and time-series-based language models (Time-series LLMs).

pages.title: Inverse Reasoning Models for Efficient Post-Training and Verification from Answer-Only Data
pages.what_its_about: A study on an inverse reasoning model-based self-distillation technique that treats reasoning paths as latent variables to perform efficient post-training and verification using answer-only data.
key_points: A framework was proposed that enables offline self-distillation even with answer-only data by utilizing a partner inverse reasoning LLM that generates backward reasoning paths conditioned on the answers.
In experiments using the Qwen3-0.6B model, a single round of offline distillation nearly doubled the pass@1 accuracy on challenging problems, even after GRPO training had saturated.
The trained inverse reasoning model functions as an accurate verifier at test time, significantly improving selection accuracy in best-of-n sampling compared to majority voting.
notable_data_or_quotes: Qwen3-0.6B
In the Countdown task during best-of-n testing, selection accuracy improved from 0.753 with majority voting to 0.969
pages.intended_audience: AI researchers and machine learning engineers studying LLM reasoning post-training and reinforcement learning efficiency techniques.

pages.title: PMO-Dock: Benchmarking Docking, Specificity, and Generalization in Molecular Optimization
pages.what_its_about: This paper proposes PMO-Dock, a novel molecular optimization benchmark designed to reflect structure-based drug discovery settings and fairly evaluate docking, target specificity, and generalization performance on unseen tasks.
key_points: Overcoming the limitations of conventional PMO benchmarks based solely on simple physical properties, PMO-Dock establishes 25 docking tasks that encompass hit discovery, lead optimization, and target specificity tasks accounting for off-target interaction penalties.

To reflect realistic drug discovery settings, a standardized protocol was introduced with strict oracle call budget constraints and a clear separation between validation tasks for hyperparameter tuning and test tasks for final evaluation.

Benchmarking four optimization paradigms—reinforcement learning (Saturn), discrete diffusion models (GenMol), genetic-guided GFlowNet, and LLM-based evolutionary search (ChemLlama)—revealed that no single model consistently outperformed others across all tasks, highlighting the need for tailored strategies per methodology due to hyperparameter transferability limits.
notable_data_or_quotes: 25 tasks
Saturn (reinforcement learning), GenMol (discrete diffusion), Genetic-guided GFlowNet, and ChemLlama (LLM-based evolutionary search)
pages.intended_audience: Researchers in AI-driven drug discovery and developers of structural biology/molecular optimization models

pages.title: Scaling Cheap Synthetic Pretraining Improves Indoor Radio-Map Prediction
pages.what_its_about: This study significantly improves indoor radio-frequency path loss (Radio-Map) prediction performance by pretraining on large-scale, low-cost synthetic data leveraging diverse indoor layout generators and a fast open-source ray tracer.
key_points: To address the high cost of real-world measurement data and precision ray-tracing simulations, the researchers introduced an indoor layout generator and a fast approximate ray tracer to build a large-scale synthetic dataset of 128M samples.

After pretraining and fine-tuning ResNet-101 and Swin-T encoder-decoder models, the ResNet-101 model reduced the average error by 15% across five indoor radio-map prediction tasks compared to prior state-of-the-art methods, while also improving transfer performance on small-scale real-world measurements.

Using a power-law fit on 2M to 16M samples, the average normalized RMSE across the 32M to 128M range was predicted with high accuracy (a MAPE of 3.33% for ResNet-101), confirming clear data scaling laws.

pages.title: IR-PRM+ with Previous-Utility Prediction: Constant Regret and Best-Iterate Convergence
pages.what_its_about: This study achieves constant regret and best-iterate convergence guarantees in two-player zero-sum games using the IR-PRM+ algorithm combined with a previous-utility prediction technique.
key_points: By introducing previous-utility prediction into IR-PRM+, which supports simultaneous and alternating updates, the theoretical convergence guarantees of the conventional extragradient method were secured.
It proves a T-independent external regret upper bound, an O(T^{-1}) average duality gap, an O(T^{-1/2}) best-iterate gap, and demonstrates convergence to Nash equilibrium.

By jointly analyzing the relative growth rate of non-decreasing regret vector norms, unbounded divergence of norms is prevented, and this is extended to the CFR variant IR-PCFR+ and extensive-form games.

pages.title: Following the Flow the Law Requires: Training Voice Agents to Transfer to Unseen Regulated Procedures in Debt Collection
pages.what_its_about: This research presents a framework for training voice AI agents to strictly adhere to legally regulated conversational procedures, such as debt collection, even in novel regulatory environments not encountered during prior training.
key_points: Proposed 'FlowSpec,' a machine-readable specification that defines guideline generation, tool control, supervision, and testing to ensure agents comply with statutory and creditor-specific procedures in heavily regulated domains.

Fine-tuned a 9-billion-parameter (9B) model using 2,506 conversational datasets generated across 297 randomized procedures, evaluating it on four unseen Thai outbound call procedures (three debt collection, one non-debt).

Training results demonstrated a significant increase in procedural compliance (Documented checks) from 67–71% to 93–100%, alongside a substantial improvement in scenario pass rate from 15/43 to 40/43.

pages.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Multilingual Abstractive Summarization: A Comprehensive Study of English and Bengali
pages.what_its_about: A comprehensive comparative study evaluating the multilingual abstractive summarization performance and factual consistency of major large language models across English and Bengali, a low-resource language.
key_points: Analyzed the zero-shot performance of eight commercial and open-source LLMs on equally sized English and Bengali XL-Sum test sets by combining lexical and semantic metrics, factuality verification, and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.

In contrast to GPT-5.6 Luna, which showed strong performance across English metrics, distinct cross-lingual performance disparities were identified: LLaMA 3.3 70B recorded the highest ROUGE and BLEU scores in Bengali, while Gemini 2.5 Flash achieved the highest factuality score in Bengali.

Model rankings varied significantly depending on the evaluation methodology, demonstrating the limitations of relying on a single evaluation metric and proving that superior performance in English does not directly transfer to low-resource languages.

pages.title: Can LLMs Access their World Knowledge for Event Prediction?
pages.what_its_about: This study presents interface design methodologies and a benchmark to help Large Language Models (LLMs) effectively leverage their extensive pre-trained knowledge for time-series event prediction.
key_points: It identifies that the poor performance of LLMs in event prediction stems not from a lack of knowledge, but from limitations in how input and output interfaces are designed.

It proposes two interface design principles: linking each event to a natural language description, and decoupling the semantic meaning of events from the prediction space to prevent bias caused by label association.

By establishing and evaluating on DescribeEvent, a new benchmark comprising approximately 150,000 events across seven datasets and six domains, high-performing LLMs achieved superior prediction performance compared to non-LLM baselines and existing methods.

pages.title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Decoding
pages.what_its_about: This study proposes JSSA, a token-level joint subspace-based sparse attention method designed to accelerate long-context large language model (LLM) decoding.
key_points: Implements precise token-level sparse attention by learning a shared low-dimensional query-key subspace that minimizes token score preservation error
Develops a gather-free indexed attention kernel supporting independent per-KV-head selection in GQA layouts and eliminating gather operation overhead
Significantly enhances decoding throughput while preserving full KV cache-level accuracy across standard GQA, sliding window, and MLA models

Achieves inference accuracy comparable to model-native DSA without additional model training, and reaches 96–99% of decoding throughput even on 700B-scale models

pages.title: Pre-Trained Language Models as Zero-Shot Tools for Social Science Research

key_points: It introduces the EnsembleLink algorithm, which combines pre-trained embeddings with string-based scoring to retrieve candidates and find optimal matches, achieving superior generalization across diverse writing systems and formats.
In name-based ethnicity inference using U.S. voter data, LLMs achieved up to 83.8% accuracy, outperforming the conventional name-supplemented BISG method (78.0%).
LLMs are also applicable to inferring religion, caste, and other ethnic groups outside the United States, effectively mitigating bias in estimating geographic racial disparities.

pages.title: Why AI Confidence Is Not Validation

pages.title: OpenAI Strikes Back in Apple Trade Secret Lawsuit: "Our Confidential Data Was Leaked Too"
pages.what_its_about: OpenAI has retaliated against Apple's trade secret infringement lawsuit, claiming that a former employee who returned to Apple leaked confidential files concerning its unreleased AI devices.
key_points: OpenAI claimed in court that a former employee who returned to Apple leaked over 100 confidential files regarding unreleased AI hardware, hinting at a potential countersuit.
Apple had previously filed a lawsuit in July alleging that former employees, including Tang Tan who moved to OpenAI, leaked trade secrets, but Apple flatly denied OpenAI's latest retaliatory claims.

The two companies, which formed a partnership in 2024, have entered into a legal dispute as competition intensifies with OpenAI's full-scale development of hardware such as smart speakers and Apple's expansion into home AI devices.
